analysis: Examined the two changed files. (1) ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift:106 now has persistLoadedModelSet() return early when addonHoldActive is true, so a temporary add-on-hold unload does not overwrite the persisted loaded-model plan (LoadedModelsStore). The plan is only an operator-local list of model IDs and is not a secret. The startup preload plan still filters through advertisedModels, so a stale persisted ID cannot cause an unadvertised model to load. Impact is limited to availability and warmup (A-018, T-059, TB-012). Residual concern: a same-UID local process able to trigger a hold could keep the persisted plan stale for the hold's duration. That is within the T-059 accepted same-user boundary, and the plan is rewritten on the next non-hold load or unload. addonHoldActive is not defined in the supplied evidence; its semantics (cleared on release and crash paths) should be confirmed in the integration pass, since a stuck flag would stop persistence. (2) ProviderLoop.swift:493-502 adds only state declarations: addonHoldSettleTimeout, which references ProviderLoop.addonHoldSettleTimeoutDefault (not visible in the supplied units), and an internal test-only hook, addonHoldBeforeCancellingStragglersForTesting, which is nil in production. The hook is `internal`, not a public or production-reachable seam, and it adds no new attack surface. The new settle timeout and its use are not shown, so the hold, release and drain logic cannot be assessed here. No change touches crypto, attestation, authorization, the coordinator wire contract, or the cache (T-041). No regression was identified. Remaining question for integration: confirm how addonHoldSettleTimeout is consumed elsewhere in the PR and that addonHoldActive clears reliably.
